definition: React Routing is a core concept in MERN Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What React Routing is
theory.body: React Routing describes the methods and patterns used within MERN Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: React Routing is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why React Routing matters
theory.body: Without React Routing, systems built with MERN Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How React Routing works
theory.body: The mechanism behind React Routing follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of React Routing.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of React Routing
theory.body: React Routing offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
